extracted.intended_audience: readers and scholars of Montaigne; editors/translators of classical texts; Project Gutenberg users/distributors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical/legal requirements relevant to producing, editing, and distributing a published edition of a classical work (here, Montaigne’s Essays) and distributing it via Project Gutenberg. Covers textual-editing choices (collation, restoration, annotation, translation fidelity) and Project Gutenberg redistribution/legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-text selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor selected Cotton’s first edition (3 vols. 1685-6, republished in later impressions) as the base English text for these volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and state clearly which printed edition or translation will serve as the base text for a new edition; document edition history (impressions, reprints) so readers know the textual foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collation with best original/variorum edition
rubrics_metrics.description: Cotton’s translation was carefully collated with the ‘variorum’ edition of the original (Paris, 1854, 4 vols. 8vo), and parallel passages from earlier undertakings (e.g., Florin) have occasionally been inserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should perform careful collation of the chosen translation against the best available edition(s) of the original-language text (variorum or critical editions) and, where useful, present parallel readings or alternative translations in footnotes or apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore omitted matter to preserve integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Places where the translator (Cotton) omitted material were restored to the text, since restoration of omitted matter was considered essential to the work’s integrity and completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where earlier translators/editors omitted passages, consider restoring them to the main text when they are part of the author’s work; document restorations and justify them in editorial notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate translator interpolations rather than leaving them in text
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor considered Cotton’s habit of inserting paragraphs/words to ‘elucidate or strengthen’ the author’s meaning a transgression; such interpolations were either cancelled or moved into notes rather than allowed to stand in Montaigne’s text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a translator has introduced explanatory or modernizing interpolations, place such material in the notes (or mark it clearly) rather than presenting it as the original author’s wording; be transparent about editorial interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify and retranslate corrupted or loose quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations in Cotton’s English versions were 'singularly loose and inexact'; the editor verified and retransmitted these quotations, aided by collation with the French edition and assistance from a previous editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check all quoted material against the original-language sources; retranslate or correct loose/inaccurate quotations and document changes in footnotes or commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-by-line/word-by-word collation with best edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor and his collaborator collated the English text 'line for line and word for word' with the best French edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform meticulous, granular collation (line/word level) when preparing an authoritative edition, and record such work in the preface or editorial apparatus so readers understand the level of textual scrutiny applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include biographical and documentary material where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: A Life of the Author and recovered Letters (sixteen) were provided to supplement the Essays, while noting that the correspondence remains fragmentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment the text with relevant biographical materials and correspondence to situate the work historically and intellectually, but note limitations (fragmentary state) and editorial choices about inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing author's language to translator's contemporary idiom
rubrics_metrics.description: The preface criticises translators' 'propensity for reducing his language and phraseology to the language and phraseology of the age and country to which they belonged' and inserting explanatory matter; this was judged unfortunate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the original author's linguistic character where feasible rather than modernizing phrasing to the translator/editor’s contemporary idiom; if modernization is done, document and justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document editorial choices and corrections in preface/notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor documents his interventions (cancelling or moving interpolations to notes, restoring omissions, collating texts) in the preface and notes to make editorial practice transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear editorial statement (preface/apparatus) describing sources, emendations, restorations, and rationale for interventions so readers can evaluate editorial fidelity and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check local copyright law before use outside U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: The eBook is for use 'anyone anywhere in the United States and most other parts of the world' but readers not located in the United States must check the laws of their country before using the eBook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before reusing or distributing a text obtained via Project Gutenberg, verify the copyright status in your jurisdiction and obey local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep and distribute the full Project Gutenberg License with copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless references to Project Gutenberg are removed, the full Project Gutenberg License must accompany the work and the specific introductory sentence (paragraph 1.E.1) must appear prominently whenever any copy is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distributing Project Gutenberg texts, include the full license text and the required prominent sentence (with active links if online). Do not detach or remove the license terms (see 1.E.1, 1.E.4, 1.E.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg trademark use and branding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Gutenberg is a registered trademark and may only be used on or associated with an electronic work by people who agree to the terms of the license; alternatively, removing all references to Project Gutenberg allows copying without complying with the full terms (but then the Project Gutenberg name must be removed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you keep Project Gutenberg branding you must comply with the license terms; if you remove Project Gutenberg references you may redistribute more freely but must not use the trademark. Be explicit about which route you take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-conversion and original-format availability
rubrics_metrics.description: You may convert and distribute the work in many formats, but if you provide it in a format other than 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' or the official format posted, you must, at no additional cost, provide a copy or means to obtain the original 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' or official form upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offering alternative file formats, ensure users can obtain the original official/plain text version at no extra cost; include the full license with alternate formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging fees and royalty/refund obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access to Project Gutenberg works unless you comply with paragraph 1.E.8 (which requires paying a 20% royalty of gross profits to the trademark owner (donated to the Foundation), offering refunds, defect replacement, and complying with all other terms) or obtain written permission under 1.E.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you intend to charge for copies/access, follow the specified royalty, refund and defect-handling obligations or obtain explicit written permission from the Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited right of replacement or refund for defects (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover a defect in the electronic work within 90 days of receipt, you can receive a refund or replacement from the provider; replacement may be offered in lieu of refund (paragraph 1.F.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must offer defect replacement or refund remedies within the 90-day window and document the procedure; consumers should report defects promptly to obtain remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnity and disclaimer obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Distributors/users agree to indemnify and hold the Foundation and related parties harmless from liability arising from distribution, alteration, or defects caused by the user (paragraph 1.F.6); the work is provided 'AS-IS' with disclaimers of warranty (1.F.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that Project Gutenberg disclaims warranties and requires indemnification for distribution or alteration; ensure you understand and accept these legal terms before redistributing or modifying texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect additional copyright/permission terms when present
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual Project Gutenberg work is posted with the permission of the copyright holder, redistribution must comply with both Project Gutenberg terms and any additional terms imposed by the copyright holder (1.E.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the specific work includes any extra permissions or restrictions from the copyright holder and comply with those in addition to the Project Gutenberg License.
